prompt: $p$ friends share a pizza equally. Each gets $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the pizza. How many friends?
hint: When a whole is shared equally, the size of each share tells you how many shares there are.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Suppose each friend got $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the pizza. Four quarters make a whole, so there would be $4$ friends. Use the same idea with eighths.
When a whole is shared equally, the size of each share tells you how many shares there are.
With $p$ friends each share is $\dfrac{1}{p}$, so $\dfrac{1}{p} = \dfrac{1}{8}$. Find how many eighths make one whole pizza.
Eight shares of $\dfrac{1}{8}$ make one whole, so there are $8$ friends.

explanation: Sharing one pizza equally among $p$ friends gives each friend $\dfrac{1}{p}$ of it.
Each share is $\dfrac{1}{8}$, so the equation is $\dfrac{1}{p} = \dfrac{1}{8}$.
Two unit fractions are equal only when their denominators match, so $p = 8$.
There are $8$ friends, and $8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 1$ whole pizza confirms it.

alternativeExplanations.title: Eighths fit into a whole
steps: So $8$ friends each get one eighth.
